picks.title: MUSEBENCH: A Benchmark for AI-Generated Music Detection and Artifact Analysis
picks.rationale: A 361K-track benchmark tests 11 AI-music detectors against Suno/Udio and 8 other generators and names the artifacts that give them away. This is the detection layer behind the labelling push now under way at YouTube Music, Deezer and Qobuz.
picks.excerpt: A 361K-track benchmark (human, Suno/Udio and eight other generators, human-AI co-creations, perturbed variants) tests 11 AI-music detectors. It identifies telltale artifacts such as non-idiomatic harmony, upsampling spectral periodicities and physically impossible performances.

picks.title: Point-and-Play: Instrument Timbre Cloning from Music Mixtures
picks.rationale: Clones a cued instrument's timbre directly from a full mix, with no stem separation, and plays it at new pitches and velocities. It is a new method, separate from the LiveSynth paper published 10-13, and gives producers a sample-to-instrument workflow.
picks.excerpt: A system that clones a cued instrument's timbre straight from a fully mixed recording, skipping stem separation, and plays it at new pitches and velocities. It beats separate-then-clone baselines.

picks.title: Sen. Marsha Blackburn Slammed for 'Cringe' AI Video of Her as Kendrick Lamar Performing 'Not Like Us' at Super Bowl
picks.rationale: A sitting U.S. senator, and a lead voice on AI likeness legislation, posted an AI video that puts her into Kendrick Lamar's Super Bowl performance. It is a concrete new case of artist-likeness use in AI media.
picks.excerpt: U.S. Sen. Marsha Blackburn was criticised on social media for posting an AI video of herself performing Kendrick Lamar's "Not Like Us" at the Super Bowl. The item is about AI music likeness and deepfakes.

picks.title: What Should Music Awards Recognize in the Age of AI?
picks.rationale: Proposes judging the human creative decisions behind AI-assisted work and asks awards bodies to adopt AI-disclosure rules. It is a framework argument, not a news event, and is distinct from the 09-20 AI Music Awards story.
picks.excerpt: An opinion piece arguing that awards should judge the human creative decisions behind AI-assisted work, and that awards bodies need transparency rules on AI use.
